cards.name: Effect Gallery
cards.summary: Opens the Effect Gallery: the Photoshop Filter Gallery dialog inside Illustrator, with every Artistic, Brush Strokes, Distort (gallery), Sketch, Stylize (Glowing Edges) and Texture effect in one previewing window; the chosen filter is applied as that filter's own live effect (the harvest opened on the last used filter, Stamp, and stored LiveEffect PSAdapter_plugin_Stmp).
use_for: browsing painterly / sketch / texture looks on vector art before committing to one
turning a flat illustration into a poster with a hand-made texture
previewing several gallery filters on the same object with one dialog
avoid: scripted pipelines: there is no live-effect name for the gallery itself; apply the chosen filter's own PSAdapter_plugin_<code> live effect instead
crisp print logos and small type: the result is a raster at the document raster resolution, edges soften and small type loses its crisp outline (the text itself stays editable under the effect)
flat single-colour fills with most painterly filters: they need tonal variation (gradients, placed photos) to show

params.name: Effect
params.does: which gallery filter is applied (each has its own sliders in the dialog); the harvest's dialog opened on the last used one
params.typical: Cutout / Colored Pencil / Glowing Edges / Halftone Pattern for a strong graphic look

pairs_with: Effect > Document Raster Effects Settings (resolution first)
Appearance panel (re-edit or stack several gallery effects)
Object > Expand Appearance to bake the raster
cards.scripting: app.executeMenuCommand("Live PSAdapter_plugin_GEfc") on the selection: opens the modal Effect Gallery dialog, which a person (or a posted Enter) must confirm; for a chosen filter use that filter's pageItem.applyEffect('<LiveEffect name="PSAdapter_plugin_<code>">...')
cards.cost: 0 cr, local; slower to redraw on large art at 300 ppi

review.changes: avoid: 'type stops being editable-looking' reworded (type under a live effect stays editable; only its rendering rasterizes)

verified.note: On the photo plate the filter the gallery stores (Glowing Edges, LiveEffect PSAdapter_plugin_GlwE) turns everything black with thin glowing coloured edges along every contour, the strip blocks reduced to coloured outlines, so the Effect Gallery applied its chosen filter as that filter's own effect, as the card says.

cards.name: Colored Pencil
cards.summary: Redraws the art as coloured-pencil hatching on a solid paper colour: edges keep rough cross-hatched strokes in the object's colours while smooth flat areas give way to the paper (harvest render of the scripted apply, sent without the parameter block: a flat red box turned flat mid-grey paper with a thin pencilled edge).
use_for: hand-drawn / sketchbook look on a flat illustration or icon set
kids' book or school-theme poster art
softening a vector mascot into a pencil study
avoid: large flat fills you want to keep their colour: they become paper colour, use Effect > Artistic > Rough Pastels or a pencil-textured brush stroke instead
tiny type: hatching eats thin letters

expecting the same look at another raster resolution: Illustrator rasterizes it at Effect > Document Raster Effects Settings (the harvest dialog ran at PrevDres 300), and its pixel sizes are fixed in pixels, so the same values look finer at 300 ppi than at 72 ppi

a plain scripted applyEffect cannot set this effect's own sliders: the Photoshop parameter block (binary 'data') cannot be sent in Dict data; set them in the dialog (executeMenuCommand), start from a graphic style that already holds them, or use the gallery route (see scripting), which renders the chosen values pixel-identical to the dialog

params.name: Pencil Width
params.does: thickness of the pencil strokes
params.typical: 4 (dialog value at harvest); 8-12 for clearly visible strokes at 300 ppi

params.name: Stroke Pressure
params.does: how dark/strong the pencil strokes are
params.typical: 8 (dialog value at harvest); 12-14 for dark strokes

params.name: Paper Brightness
params.does: tone of the paper that replaces smooth areas (low = dark paper, high = near white)
params.typical: 25 (dialog value at harvest); 40-45 for near-white paper

pairs_with: Effect > Stylize > Scribble (vector hatching alternative)
a paper texture placed under at Multiply
cards.scripting: pageItem.applyEffect('<LiveEffect name="PSAdapter_plugin_ClrP"><Dict data="I dataSize 68 I PrevDres 300 B go 1"/></LiveEffect>'); with the dialog instead: app.executeMenuCommand("Live PSAdapter_plugin_ClrP") on the selection (opens the modal dialog). Gallery route (2026-10-13): a plain applyEffect cannot carry the dialog settings (the Photoshop parameter block is binary 'data' that Dict data cannot send); the gallery applies the effect, saves the file, writes the dialog's parameter dictionary into it and reopens it, and that route renders the chosen values pixel-identical to the dialog (Dark Strokes control).

verified.note: The photo is redrawn as rough coloured-pencil cross-hatching on light paper: contours and textured areas keep hatched strokes in their own colours while the smooth flat strip blocks turn to paper with only a coloured pencilled edge, as the summary describes.

avoid: thin strokes, hairlines and small type: Edge Simplicity merges them away
when you need real vector shapes: Object > Expand Appearance, then Object > Image Trace on the raster (Cutout itself stays a raster)

avoid: flat single-colour vector shapes: almost no visible change (Palette Knife and Paint Daubs barely change flat fills either); use a painterly Art brush on the outline, or give the fill a gradient first

cards.name: Film Grain

use_for: retro / analog grain over flat vector posters
breaking up gradient banding in large gradients
matching vector art to grainy photos in one layout
avoid: clean corporate or UI art: the grain is a raster texture that also prints
when you need noise you can move independently: place a grain texture object at Overlay instead

expecting the same look at another raster resolution: Illustrator rasterizes it at Effect > Document Raster Effects Settings (the harvest dialog ran at PrevDres 300), and its pixel sizes are fixed in pixels, so the same values look finer at 300 ppi than at 72 ppi

flat vector fills: besides the grain it scales every colour without a channel at 255 (on the flat vector plate the gradient went to about x0.62) while fills with a full channel keep their colour; that is Illustrator's own result, so judge it on a photo or textured art

cards.name: Fresco
cards.summary: Repaints the art in a coarse fresco style with short, rounded, hastily applied dabs and darkened, high-contrast shadows (on the photo plate the dark areas go near-black while the saturated colour strip survives). On flat vector art it has nothing to stroke and only remaps brightness: at the demo values every colour without a channel at 255 (the harvest's flat red box, the test plate's gradient) came out solid black, which a dialog-applied control showed is Illustrator's own result, not a script-route fault.
use_for: gritty painted poster or album art from a placed photo
aged mural / wall-painting feel on a gradient illustration
avoid: light, airy art: it darkens and adds contrast; use Effect > Artistic > Dry Brush or Paint Daubs for a lighter painterly look

expecting the same look at another raster resolution: Illustrator rasterizes it at Effect > Document Raster Effects Settings (the harvest dialog ran at PrevDres 300), and its pixel sizes are fixed in pixels, so the same values look finer at 300 ppi than at 72 ppi

flat vector fills: on flat or very smooth art this filter has nothing to stroke and only remaps brightness, so at these values every colour without a channel at 255 (gradients, dark greys, a flat red) goes solid black while fills with a full channel (pure orange, pure blue) survive; that is Illustrator's own result (a dialog-applied control matched the scripted render pixel for pixel), so give it a photo or textured art
